one_line: Solid editorial day undermined by a pervasive take scaffold and three factual errors.

findings.quote: Fraudsters used AI-generated voice to steal €95 million from Intesa Sanpaolo with no systems breach.
findings.instruction: The story summary hedges 'AI-generated voice or messaging'; the digest sentence asserts only voice. Rewrite to preserve the hedge: e.g. 'Fraudsters used AI-generated voice or messaging to steal €95 million from Intesa Sanpaolo's private banking arm, with no systems breach.'

findings.quote: Open-weight frontier coding agents required proprietary APIs; Meta's 816B model puts that capability on your own hardware.
findings.instruction: The verification block flags 'Open-weight frontier coding agents required proprietary APIs' as unsupported — the source does not assert that open-weight frontier coding agents previously required proprietary APIs. Remove or soften the historical premise. Rewrite to state only what the source supports, e.g. 'Meta's 816B open-weight model brings frontier-class agentic coding to self-hosted hardware for the first time at this scale.'

findings.quote: Run a 120-billion-parameter vision model locally on a 24GB GPU
findings.instruction: The headline implies the 120B (Super) model fits a 24GB GPU, but the body states only the smaller Bolt variant (74B parameters, 9B active) fits a 24GB GPU. Rewrite the headline to name the Bolt variant and its actual parameter count, e.g. 'Run Nemotron 3.5 Bolt, a 74-billion-parameter vision model, locally on a 24GB GPU'.

findings.quote: When does your credit team pilot this against its own policy library?
findings.instruction: Big Picture bodies must close on a strategic question anchored to a specific role, decision, or constraint — not a prescription dressed as a question. 'When does your credit team pilot this' is a call to action, not a strategic question. Rewrite to surface a genuine decision point, e.g. 'Does your credit team's policy library exist in a form this prototype could ingest, or is the extraction step the real bottleneck?'

findings.quote: Three preprints and one infrastructure release share a common direction
findings.instruction: The Currents section contains two arXiv preprints (c_2d600bb678cfaee4 and c_e77b27d7f15326c1) and one vendor blog/infrastructure release (c_e8f570b0ce6c55ee), not three preprints. Correct to 'Two preprints and one infrastructure release share a common direction'.

findings.quote: Serverless networking required per-resource proxy deployments; one delegated subnet now covers everything.
findings.instruction: Six takes in this issue share the scaffold '[X] required [Y]; [new thing] now [does Z]': the Pulse take, c_21edd24076e9ed8a, c_58c513853fc76164, c_2d600bb678cfaee4, c_e77b27d7f15326c1, and this one. Three or more sharing a frame is a major defect. Rewrite this take (and at least two others) to break the pattern. For this story, try a frame that names the operational change directly, e.g. 'Private Network Gateway collapses Databricks serverless connectivity into a single delegated subnet, removing the per-resource proxy layer.'

findings.quote: Private Network Gateway replaces per-resource load balancers and proxy VMs with a single delegated subnet, routing all serverless traffic through your existing firewall.
findings.instruction: This story covers general cloud networking infrastructure with no financial-services framing. The FS angle is absent from the summary and take. Arman should confirm whether this story belongs in the issue or whether a sentence anchoring the relevance to FS data-governance or compliance requirements should be added.

note: verdict rule: major >= 3 (Three substantive editorial defects is not three fixes, it is a draft that did not come out right. Re-summarise beats patching.)
